title: The Cool evening in the hills
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：cool　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cool 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the director wrote of ① a cool evening in the hills in the poster, and everybody in the theatre said at once that it was ② cooler than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the director, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the cool ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the coolest evening in the hills anybody in the theatre had ever seen, or so the poster for August 1965 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too cool to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the actor who had come to help; the cool ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a cool reply to the threat, and said that no actor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as cool as the reply to the threat they had once had in the old theatre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was cool or not, and he said so.

By 1978 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the poster. What the line asked for was ⑦ something cool, and nothing besides. The actor from the next theatre called the whole plan ⑧ quite cool; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the poster kept the names of the cool ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1981, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another cool evening in the hills in the same poster, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ cooler than anybody had expected. ⑩ The coolest reply to the threat in the whole theatre, she said in 1983, was the one she could never quite name; the cool ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 凉爽（前置定语 a cool evening in the hills：1971 年导演在戏报里记下的那件凉爽的傍晚）
B. adj. 凉爽／冷静（比较级 cooler than：文中两处，一处比山里的傍晚，一处比预想）
C. adj. 凉爽／冷静（最高级 the coolest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 凉爽（表语 too cool to do：母亲觉得它太凉爽，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 冷静（前置定语 a cool reply to the threat：叔叔把整件事称作一桩冷静的回应）
F. adj. 冷静（同级比较 as cool as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩面对威胁的回应相比）
G. adj. 冷静（后置定语 something cool：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 冷静（受程度副词修饰 quite cool：那位演员的评价）

items.q: a cool evening in the hills
the coolest evening in the hills anybody
a cool reply to the threat
The coolest reply to the threat in

answers.why: cool 意为“凉爽”，1971 年导演在戏报里记下的是“一件凉爽的傍晚”，此处作前置定语 a cool evening in the hills。
cool 意为“凉爽”，此处用比较级 cooler than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
cool 意为“凉爽”，戏报上 八月 那行字说它是戏院里最凉爽的一件，故用最高级 the coolest evening in the hills。
cool 意为“凉爽”，母亲认为这件东西“太凉爽了，谁也用不上”，too cool to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
cool 意为“冷静”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩冷静的回应”，此处作前置定语 a cool reply to the threat。
cool 意为“冷静”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩面对威胁的回应一样冷静”，同级比较用 as cool as。
cool 意为“冷静”，戏报上那半行字要的是“冷静的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something cool。
cool 意为“冷静”，邻戏院来的那位演员认为这套计划“相当冷静”，quite 修饰原级 cool。
cool 意为“冷静”，1981 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要冷静”，故用比较级 cooler than。
cool 意为“冷静”，母亲 1983 年说的是“整个戏院里最冷静的那一桩”，故用最高级 the coolest reply to the threat。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1971 年，导演在戏报里记下了一件凉爽的傍晚。（a cool evening in the hills）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更凉爽。（cooler than …）
母亲觉得它太凉爽，谁也用不上。（too cool to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩冷静的回应。（a cool reply to the threat）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩面对威胁的回应一样冷静。（as cool as …）
到了 1978 年，戏报上只剩半行字：要的是一件冷静的东西。（something cool）
answers: In 1971 the director wrote of a cool evening in the hills in the poster.
Everybody said it was cooler than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too cool to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a cool reply to the threat.
He said nobody would call it as cool as the reply to the threat they had once had.
By 1978 the poster asked for nothing but something cool.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 cool 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1971 the director wrote of a cool evening in the hills in the poster, and nobody forgot it.
It was the coolest evening in the hills in the theatre, or so the poster says.
My mother thought it too cool to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a cool reply to the threat, and nobody argued with him.
The actor from the next theatre called the plan quite cool, and everybody laughed.
The cool ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
